notes: All six candidates are software. Metadata came from the GitHub REST API (repo JSON: created_at, pushed_at, license, description). A later README call via the unauthenticated API hit the rate limit, so READMEs, LICENSE, AUTHORS and CITATION files were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com/<owner>/<repo>/HEAD/ and source trees were listed with authenticated gh api git/trees. Also used: PyPI JSON API (version, author, license, release upload times), the DataCite API for the BluePyEfe DOI, and Crossref plus Europe PMC for the paper NetworkUnit's docs ask users to cite. Years for GitHub-only records are repository creation years, not release or publication years. License inconsistencies: (a) ipfx - GitHub reports NOASSERTION, the PyPI classifier is Other/Proprietary, and the LICENSE file is an Allen Institute licence (BSD-2 plus a clause forbidding commercial redistribution without permission); (b) pyelectro - GitHub API says BSD-3-Clause but the PyPI license field says BSD-2-clause; (c) BluePyEfe - LGPL-3.0 per DataCite, the PyPI classifier and LICENSE.txt, while GitHub reports NOASSERTION. No candidate was rejected: all exist and no metadata conflicts were irreconcilable.

rows.citation: Gutzen R, von Papen M, Denker M, et al. (2017). NetworkUnit: a SciUnit library for validation testing of spiking neural network models. GitHub software (INM-6/networkunit; PyPI networkunit 0.2.2).
rows.model_type: spiking neural network models (population activity / spike-train data, e.g. NEST simulations and SpiNNaker reproductions); not single-cell conductance models
rows.controlled_mutations: no - README and docs describe statistical validation tests and scores; no mutant generation or seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - tests compare spike-train statistics of network activity; no battery of current-clamp stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - network-level spiking statistics (firing rates, ISI CV, correlations, power spectra), not single-cell eFEL-style features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - fixed library of test and score classes chosen by the user; no selection of a compact test set.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no discovery/held-out split of models or fault families described in README or docs.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.software: NetworkUnit - https://github.com/INM-6/networkunit (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API; PyPI 0.2.2, last upload 2024-01-04)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Precedent for model-to-model equivalence testing between implementations, e.g. a simulator reproduction, at network level. NeuroSem targets single-cell NeuroML edits and adds mutants, stimulation-protocol batteries, refinement-calibrated tolerances, compact battery selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo JSON (created 2017-11-14, BSD-3-Clause, description); raw README.rst, AUTHORS.txt and doc/citing.rst; PyPI JSON (0.2.2, first release 0.1.0 on 2018-11-06). The paper cited in doc/citing.rst was checked on Crossref (api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/fninf.2018.00090: Gutzen, von Papen, Trensch, Quaglio, Grun, Denker; Front Neuroinform 12:90; 2018) and its abstract read on Europe PMC (PMID 30618696): it validates a network model against its SpiNNaker reproduction.
rows.found_via: GitHub search sciunit; PyPI JSON networkunit 0.2.2

rows.citation: Rössert C, Van Geit W, Iavarone E, et al. (2026). BluePyEfe (version 2.3.63). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19591682
rows.model_type: experimental intracellular voltage recordings (patch-clamp traces) used as feature targets for detailed neuron model building with BluePyOpt
rows.controlled_mutations: no - extracts features from recordings; no model edits or seeded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - handles several named protocols per cell; amplitudes are expressed as a percentage of each cell's rheobase.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - extracts eFEL e-features and averages them across equivalent traces and cells.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - protocols and features are user-configured; no selection of an informative subset.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no model or fault held-out evaluation; it is a data-processing tool.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.software: BluePyEfe - https://github.com/openbraininstitute/BluePyEfe (LGPL-3.0 per DataCite and PyPI classifier; PyPI 2.3.63)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Reusable component: multi-protocol, rheobase-normalised eFEL feature targets from data. NeuroSem compares a model against its edited version and adds mutants, tolerance calibration, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API api.datacite.org/dois/10.5281/zenodo.19591682 (title, 11 creators, publicationYear 2026, version 2.3.63, LGPL-3.0); raw CITATION.cff (same author list, date-released 2020-03-01) and README.rst (rheobase-normalised protocol equivalence, pseudo-code); GitHub REST API repo JSON; PyPI JSON (2.3.63 uploaded 2026-08-24; first release 0.1.3 in 2020).
rows.found_via: GitHub search bluepyefe; CITATION.cff; DataCite API; PyPI bluepyefe 2.3.63

rows.citation: Allen Institute for Brain Science (2017). IPFX: Intrinsic Physiology Feature Extractor. GitHub software (AllenInstitute/ipfx; PyPI ipfx 2.1.2).
rows.model_type: experimental whole-cell intracellular electrophysiology recordings (NWB datasets); not a model-testing tool
rows.controlled_mutations: no - README and docs cover data QC and feature computation; no mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - a stimulus ontology tags sweeps by type (e.g. short and long square) and computes stimulus-specific cell features.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - action-potential and spike-train features such as threshold and adaptation index, plus stimulus-specific features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection or optimisation of stimulus sets; the ontology only maps and filters recorded sweeps.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out model or fault evaluation.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.software: IPFX - https://github.com/AllenInstitute/ipfx (Allen Institute Software License: BSD-2 plus non-commercial redistribution clause; GitHub NOASSERTION; PyPI 2.1.2)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Possible alternative feature extractor; its licence restricts commercial redistribution. NeuroSem's contribution is not feature extraction but mutation-calibrated regression testing with selected protocols and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo JSON (created 2017-12-10, license NOASSERTION); raw README.md, LICENSE, AUTHORS.rst and docs/stimuli.rst; ipfx.readthedocs.io landing page; PyPI JSON (2.1.2 uploaded 2025-12-10, classifier Other/Proprietary, author Allen Institute for Brain Science).
rows.found_via: GitHub search ipfx electrophysiology; PyPI JSON ipfx 2.1.2

rows.citation: Vella M, Gleeson P (2013). pyelectro: a Python library for analysis of electrophysiological data. GitHub software (NeuralEnsemble/pyelectro; PyPI pyelectro 0.2.7).
rows.model_type: voltage traces from recordings or simulations (current-clamp and network analyses); used with OpenWorm and Open Source Brain projects
rows.controlled_mutations: no - analysis functions only; no model mutation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - analyses a given trace window; no stimulation-protocol battery defined.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - spike detection, frequencies, widths, adaptation, bursting and phase-plane measures via IClampAnalysis and helper functions.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.software: pyelectro - https://github.com/NeuralEnsemble/pyelectro (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API; PyPI license field says BSD-2-clause; PyPI 0.2.7)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: NeuroML-community trace-feature library; a possible complement to eFEL. It provides no regression, mutation, tolerance calibration or protocol selection, all of which NeuroSem would add.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo JSON (created 2013-08-26, BSD-3-Clause); raw README.md and LICENSE; gh api git tree plus function listing of pyelectro/analysis.py; pyelectro.readthedocs.io landing page; PyPI JSON (0.2.7 uploaded 2023-06-22, authors Michael Vella and Padraig Gleeson).
rows.found_via: GitHub search pyelectro; PyPI JSON pyelectro 0.2.7

rows.citation: Vella M, Gleeson P (2012). Neurotune: a Python library for optimising neuronal models. GitHub software (NeuralEnsemble/neurotune; PyPI neurotune 0.2.6).
rows.model_type: conductance-based neuron and small network models (examples use NEURON .mod channels; GitHub description names NeuroML models)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - varies free parameters as optimisation candidates to fit targets; no single-fault mutants for test evaluation.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - IClampEvaluator scores one analysis window per candidate; no multi-protocol battery found in docs or code.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - fitness uses pyelectro IClampAnalysis feature targets, set manually or taken automatically from a reference trace, with a normalised cost.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - optimises model parameters with an evolutionary optimiser, not stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - no held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses feature-target distance between a model and a reference trace for fitting. NeuroSem would reuse similar comparisons to detect behavioural drift after edits, adding mutants, calibrated tolerances, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo JSON (created 2012-07-16, BSD-3-Clause, description); raw README.md, AUTHORS, doc/architecture.rst and neurotune/evaluators.py (IClampEvaluator read); neurotune.readthedocs.io landing page; PyPI JSON (0.2.6 uploaded 2023-05-12, authors Michael Vella and Padraig Gleeson).
rows.found_via: GitHub search neurotune; PyPI JSON neurotune 0.2.6

rows.citation: bozelosp (2026). Ion Channel Genealogy Visualizer. GitHub software (bozelosp/ion-channel-genealogy-viz).
rows.model_type: Hodgkin-Huxley ion-channel model source files (.mod) from ModelDB, catalogued by the Ion Channel Genealogy project
rows.controlled_mutations: no - observes existing reuse and modification of channel files; no generated mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - compares source code by Levenshtein similarity; no stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - Omnimodel pages show fitted steady-state and time-constant gating curves per channel; no cell-level voltage-trace features.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - an exploratory visualiser; no evaluation design.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models.
rows.software: Ion Channel Genealogy Visualizer - https://github.com/bozelosp/ion-channel-genealogy-viz (no license detected by GitHub API; no LICENSE file at HEAD); live at icg-explorer.org per README
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shows that channel code is copied and modified across publications, which motivates edit-regression testing. It compares code text and gating curves, not whole-cell behaviour under stimulation; NeuroSem would test behavioural consequences of such edits.
rows.verification_method: GitHub REST API repo JSON (created 2026-09-05, license null, description); raw README.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; gh api git tree listing (Next.js app, generation scripts); no individual author name verified beyond the GitHub owner handle.
